title: Compact controls — cross-browser spacing/regression investigation and remediation plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Several compact-density components (compact buttons, condensed table rows, and token chips) exhibit inconsistent spacing and interactive hitbox regressions across iOS Safari and Firefox on Android. The effect is most pronounced at subpixel widths and when momentum scrolling or transform-based layering is present. This ticket captures the investigation, findings, and a remediation plan that balances token stability, accessibility hitboxes, and cross-engine rendering differences.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open the UI Kit compact-density storybook on an iPhone 14 (iOS 17) in Safari: https://ui-kit.stories.redwood.local/compact
2) Navigate to 'Compact table' story and trigger a horizontal shrink by resizing window width to 360px, observe row wrap and control overlap
3) Repeat on an Android Pixel 7 using Firefox Nightly with default zoom and observe different overlap thresholds
4) In both browsers, toggle 'prefers-reduced-motion' and disable -webkit-overflow-scrolling to compare behaviors
5) Capture 3-5 frame snapshots and a short screen recording for each device/browser combination and attach to this ticket.
observed_behavior: - Compact buttons lose left/right padding by 1-3px in Safari when placed inside a transformed container (transform: translateZ(0)).
- Table row collapse in Firefox shows a 2px gap between token chips and the row divider; in Safari the chip overlaps the divider instead.
- Tap targets in compact chips are visually compressed even though computed padding remains; actual pointer hit area is shifted due to negative margins used for visual compression.
- Subpixel rounding differences across engines cause inconsistent truncation of 1px borders and token separators at certain viewport widths.
expected_behavior: - Compact density components maintain consistent visual spacing and accessible tap targets across supported browsers at all breakpoint widths.
- Visual compression should be achieved with only visual transforms or token offsets that do not reduce the pointer area or create overlap with neighboring elements.
- 1px separator/border treatments should be stable across subpixel scenarios via hairline/token rules.
investigation_findings: - Root cause is a combination of (a) token math that reduces padding by percentages at compact breakpoints, (b) use of transform: translateZ(0) in several container wrappers that promotes layers differently across engines, and (c) negative margins used to visually collapse gaps — which moves the visual box but not the hitbox consistently.
- Firefox handles subpixel rounding differently than WebKit which results in 1px separator jitter; this is amplified when border-box vs content-box assumptions differ in nested components.
- Accessibility: several compact variants rely on visual-only compression; screen reader focus and keyboard targets remained correct in testing, but touch targets were unreliable on physical devices.
- Repro rate: ~9/10 on latest Safari iOS and ~6/10 on Firefox Android across sampled component stories and pages.
design_decisions: - Normalize box-sizing to border-box at component root and enforce for all compact token children via CSS variable --rw-box-sizing.

- Stop using negative margins for pointer-area compression. Instead, introduce an explicit visual-offset CSS layer (pseudo-element) that visually compresses without changing the element's focus/hitbox.
- Introduce a small uniform hitbox token (--rw-compact-hitpad: 8px) and apply it to interactive elements to ensure minimum tappable area while preserving visual density.
- For hairline borders, add a hairline fallback token that uses transform: scaleY(0.5) with a stable background color as fallback where subpixel rounding breaks 1px separators.
- Add a browser-specific note in the docs that compact density is an accessibility-sensitive mode and requires physical-device verification before release.
proposed_work_items: 1) Design: update component tokens and docs + supply token variants for compact hitpad and hairline borders (assignee: Liam Chen) — PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ui-kit/pull/5421
2) Engineering: remove negative-margin compression from Button, Chip, TableCell and implement pseudo-element visual-offset approach (assignee: ENG-43822) — see ENG-43822 for implementation traces
3) QA: add Storybook visual tests for iOS Safari and Firefox Android snapshots via Percy (assignee: QA Squad) — depends on ENG-44110 for CI runners
4) Product: update component docs and migration notes for teams consuming the UI Kit (assignee: PM-337)
acceptance_criteria: - Compact stories show no visual overlap or lost tap targets on iOS Safari and Firefox Android at 320px, 360px, and 412px viewports.
- Visual regression snapshots pass in CI for the three defined breakpoints and both target engines.
- Token migration guide published and linked from the UI Kit README.
- No accessibility violations (WCAG) for touch target size or focus order in Lighthouse/manual checks.
